lines.text: It's 3 AM.
And your brain just remembered an email you forgot to send.
Why now?
Berlin, nineteen twenties.
A psychologist notices something odd.
Waiters remembered unpaid orders perfectly.
And forgot paid ones instantly.
At least, that's how the story goes.
Your brain does the same.
Every unfinished task stays open, like a browser tab, running quietly in the background.
And size doesn't matter.
Buying batteries nags you as loudly as changing careers.
But in twenty eleven, researchers found a loophole.
You don't have to finish the task.
You just have to make a plan.
One action. One time. One place.
Email landlord, Tuesday, nine AM, at my desk.
And the loop closes.
So tonight, don't try to remember it.
Write it down.
Then close the tabs, and sleep.
